newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil June Fipe inflation at 1.42 pct.
newsitem.headline: Brazil June Fipe inflation at 1.42 pct.

text.p: Brazil's inflation as measured by the Economic Research Institute (Fipe) was 1.42 percent in June versus 0.55 percent in May, a Fipe official said Thursday.
Fipe inflation index coordinator Juarez Rizzieri also said Fipe inflation in the 12-month period ending June 1997 totalled 7.08 percent. He did not provide comparative 12-month figures.
Rizzieri said rising telephone rates and bus fares were to blame for the marked increase in June prices over May. The Fipe index measures prices in the greater Sao Paulo area.
Fipe released the following breakdown of its weighted inflation index for June:
- Food: 0.93 pct rise in the month
- Housing: 1.90 pct rise in the month
- Transportation: 2.89 pct rise in the month
- Personal expenses: -0.12 pct drop in the month
- Clothing: 2.69 pct rise in the month
- Health care: 0.94 pct rise in the month
- Education: 0.01 pct rise in the month
The Fipe index is calculated by the University of Sao Paulo, which releases inflation figures weekly.
